Benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium) is restricted in Mexico. Legal with prescription (receta médica). Classified under Fraction III of Mexico's General Health Law. Available at pharmacies with a valid prescription.

Adderall / amphetamines is banned in Mexico. Amphetamines are Fraction I controlled substances. Adderall is not approved or available in Mexico. Importing is illegal. Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) has limited availability with specialist prescription.

Cannabis / CBD is restricted in Mexico. Mexico's Supreme Court ruled recreational use constitutional (2021). Regulatory framework still pending full implementation. Medical cannabis and CBD products are legal with COFEPRIS authorization. Personal possession of ≤5g decriminalized.

Methylphenidate (Ritalin, Concerta) is restricted in Mexico. Available by prescription for ADHD (Fraction II psychotropic). Requires a special controlled substance prescription (receta especial). Carry original packaging and prescription.

Codeine / opioids is restricted in Mexico. Codeine combinations available with prescription. Stronger opioids require special prescriptions with COFEPRIS-regulated forms. Carry documentation for travel.
Pseudoephedrine (Sudafed) is restricted in Mexico. Heavily regulated since 2008 due to methamphetamine production. Requires prescription and is tracked. OTC availability severely limited.

Psilocybin / MDMA is banned in Mexico. Both are illegal narcotics. However, traditional indigenous use of psilocybin mushrooms is culturally tolerated in certain regions (Oaxaca). No legal commercial availability.
Tramadol is restricted in Mexico. Available by prescription (Fraction IV). Standard medical prescription required. Widely available at pharmacies with valid Rx.

Tranquilizers / sleeping pills (zolpidem) is restricted in Mexico. Prescription required (Fraction IV psychotropic). Available at pharmacies with valid prescription. Carry documentation when traveling.

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — Acapulco Guerrero-State Safety Context & 'Authentic Local Tour' Risk (tourist-trap, severity: high). Acapulco is in Guerrero state — under US State Department Level 4 'Do Not Travel' advisory due to cartel violence — and 2025 tourism has only partially recovered from Hurricane Otis (Cat 5, October 2023) which devastated the city. Traveler reports from 2025 consistently flag the US State Department Level 4 advisory, and travelers and Guerrero residents both express ongoing safety concerns in 2025 threads covering the broader Mexico safety baseline. The 2025 reality: (a) Acapulco's Diamante (south, newer) and Costera (Acapulco Bay strip) tourist zones are STATISTICALLY safer than the broader city — heavy police presence, well-patrolled, cruise-port active; (b) outer Acapulco neighborhoods (Renacimiento, Zapata, Acapulco Tradicional north) have elevated cartel-related risk and are NOT recommended for tourist visits; (c) Mexico City-Acapulco highway (the 'Autopista del Sol') has documented cartel checkpoints — NOT recommended as tourist drive; fly instead; (d) Taxco day-trip from Acapulco (4-hour drive each way) crosses risky rural Guerrero — go to Taxco from Mexico City instead; (e) 'authentic local Guerrero tour' offers via Instagram/WhatsApp targeting tourists for 'rural village experience' carry real cartel-zone risk; (f) Pie de la Cuesta / Coyuca lagoon day-trip is generally safe via licensed operator but risky via informal 'beach taxi' guide. For older travelers: (1) IF visiting Acapulco, stay in Diamante or Costera zones — avoid outer neighborhoods; (2) FLY between Mexico City and Acapulco — DO NOT drive the Autopista del Sol as a tourist; one-hour Aeromexico/VivaAerobus flights are MX$1,800-3,500; (3) for Taxco visit, go from Mexico City (3-hour drive on safer highways), NOT Acapulco; (4) REFUSE every 'authentic Guerrero village tour' Instagram/WhatsApp invitation; (5) check US State Department advisory before booking (travel.state.gov/Acapulco) — Level 4 is the highest US warning tier; (6) travel insurance with full evacuation coverage is essential for Guerrero; (7) save US Embassy 24-hr emergency +52 55 8526 2561; Mexican tourist police 911 (English available); (8) Hurricane Otis recovery context: many small businesses still rebuilding 2025 — verify hotel/restaurant operating status BEFORE booking via direct phone call. How to avoid: Stay in Diamante or Costera tourist zones only FLY Mexico City-Acapulco (Aeromexico/VivaAerobus MX$1,800-3,500) Visit Taxco from Mexico City (3-hour drive), NOT from Acapulco REFUSE every 'authentic Guerrero village' tour invitation Check travel.state.gov advisory; insurance with evacuation; US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — Acapulco Airport (ACA) & Cruise-Port Taxi Mafia Overcharge (transport, severity: high). Acapulco International Airport (ACA) and the cruise port have a documented 2025 taxi-overcharge ecosystem amplified by post-Hurricane Otis tourism scarcity (drivers hungry for fares). 2025 traveler reports cover the broader Acapulco-arrival landscape and safety context. Legitimate fares: ACA airport to Costera (15 km, 25 min) via official Transporte Terrestre prepaid MX$450-600; via Uber MX$300-450 (Uber works in Acapulco but supply is THIN — wait 10-20 min); to Diamante (12 km, 20 min) MX$350-500. Cruise pier to Costera MX$200-300 via taxi; to La Quebrada cliff divers MX$300-400. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) ACA arrivals-kerb kiosks quoting MX$1,200-2,500 for Costera transfer (2-5x real); (b) 'VIP private driver' at MX$3,500 for standard sedan; (c) 'security escort fee MX$300' added after the trip (no such legitimate fee); (d) Uber driver cancelling and re-quoting cash — same pattern as CDMX/Mazatlán; (e) cruise-pier 'authorized taxi' US$50-80 for trip that's MX$200-300 metered; (f) 'combined airport + cliff divers + sunset US$250 per person' bundle marked up 4x DIY cost; (g) 'Diamante private transfer with security US$200' upsells exploiting safety fears; (h) hotel concierge kickback directing to 'recommended driver' at 2x Uber rate. Traveler reports from 2025 confirm that hotel-arranged 'travel agency' tours are essentially always scam operations. For older travelers: (1) book Uber on airport Wi-Fi after luggage — typical ACA-Costera MX$300-450 (Uber works, 10-20 min wait); (2) alternatively official Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth inside arrivals MX$450-600 (legitimate flat-rate); (3) IGNORE every arrivals-kerb kiosk quoting MX$1,200+; (4) hotel airport pickup is the safest option — most Costera/Diamante hotels include free transfer with advance booking; (5) at cruise pier, use the OFFICIAL SECTUR taxi stand (rate posted) MX$200-300 to Costera; refuse 'private US$50' offers; (6) REFUSE 'security escort fee' and 'safety surcharge' demands — illegitimate; (7) for return to ACA, pre-book Uber or Transporte Terrestre night before; (8) save Acapulco Tourist Police +52 744 484 4583 (English available) and US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561. How to avoid: Book Uber on airport Wi-Fi: ACA-Costera MX$300-450 (10-20 min wait) Or Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth MX$450-600 Use hotel free airport pickup (most include with advance booking) Cruise pier: official SECTUR taxi MX$200-300 to Costera Tourist Police +52 744 484 4583; US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — La Quebrada Cliff Divers 'Premium View' & Photo Tout Scam (tourist-trap, severity: moderate). Acapulco's La Quebrada cliff divers (clavadistas) — performing 35-meter dives into a narrow ocean inlet five times daily — is the city's iconic free public spectacle. The 2025 tout ecosystem around the show exploits tourists unfamiliar with the legitimate viewing options. Traveler reports from 2025 flag broader Acapulco tourism scams, and 2024 cruise-passenger reports cover Quebrada visits. Legitimate options: (a) FREE viewing from the public plaza (Mirador de la Quebrada) — best for the noon, 1 PM, and 7:30 PM dives; (b) El Mirador Hotel 'Coyuca 22' restaurant or 'La Perla' bar — order a drink/meal (MX$200-500) and watch from the terrace with the best angle; (c) 'official' clavadistas plaza ticket MX$50-80 for guaranteed seating during the 9:30 PM torch dive (the most spectacular). The total visit cost should be MX$50-200 per person. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'premium VIP viewing area MX$500 per person' touts at the plaza approach — no such VIP area exists at the public viewpoint; (b) 'photographer with telephoto for the dive' service quoting MX$300-800 then delivering blurry phone-photo (real professional photos are sold by the divers' association at MX$100); (c) 'private terrace reservation US$100 per person' at La Perla bar (a drink + view is MX$200 at the bar); (d) 'cliff diver meet & greet MX$400' (divers post-show take free tips MX$30-50 — no formal 'meet & greet' fee exists); (e) 'sunset cliff dive special show MX$1,000' — the 7:30 PM dive is one of the regular five daily, free to view from plaza; (f) bundled cruise-day 'Quebrada VIP + hotel transfer US$120' marking up MX$300 actual cost. For older travelers: (1) for the 7:30 PM or 9:30 PM dive, arrive 30-45 min early to get a good spot at the public plaza viewpoint (FREE); (2) for guaranteed seating, the 9:30 PM torch dive plaza ticket is MX$50-80 (sold at the gate); (3) for the BEST view, order a drink at La Perla bar (Hotel El Mirador) — MX$200 buys you a margarita and the terrace view; (4) REFUSE every 'VIP viewing area MX$500', 'private photographer MX$300', 'meet & greet MX$400' offer — none is legitimate; (5) tip individual divers post-show MX$30-50 if you want to thank them; (6) cliff-diver photographs available at the divers' association booth MX$80-100; (7) the divers' show times (varies seasonally): 1 PM, 7:30 PM, 8:30 PM, 9:30 PM, 10:30 PM — verify on quebradacliffsdivers.com; (8) Quebrada is in Old Acapulco — well-policed during show hours but take Uber back to hotel after dark. How to avoid: Arrive 30-45 min early at FREE public plaza for 7:30/9:30 PM dive Or 9:30 PM torch dive plaza ticket MX$50-80 at gate for guaranteed seat Best view: order MX$200 margarita at La Perla bar (Hotel El Mirador) REFUSE 'VIP viewing', 'private photographer', 'meet & greet' upsells Tip divers post-show MX$30-50; photos at association booth MX$80-100

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — Acapulco Diamante Resort Timeshare & 'Hurricane-Recovery' Pressure Sale (tourist-trap, severity: high). Acapulco's Diamante and Costera resort sectors host a 2025 timeshare-presentation ecosystem with a unique post-Hurricane-Otis 'rebuilding investment' angle. Traveler reports from 2025 flag hotel-pitch scams, and the US State Department Level 4 advisory context makes 'investment in Acapulco' pitches especially risky. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Diamante resort welcome desks (Princess Mundo Imperial, Vidanta Acapulco) offering 'free breakfast + US$200 credit + Diamante access' for '90-min preview'; (b) 'Acapulco rebuilding investment opportunity US$25,000+' pitched as patriotic post-Otis recovery (high-risk speculative); (c) 'fractional ownership rental yield 8-12% guaranteed' — no rental yield can be guaranteed in a USDOS Level 4 destination; (d) high-pressure 3-5 hour presentations with closer escalation; (e) 'snowbird membership US$15,000-30,000' targeting US/Canadian retirees; (f) 'cancellation fee US$500' to exit early; (g) 'celebrity endorser' name-drop tactics (Hurricane Otis recovery features prominently in pitches); (h) 'Mexican real estate fideicomiso required US$5,000 admin fee' — fideicomiso IS the legal structure for foreigner property in Mexico's restricted coastal zone, but admin fees are normally MX$10,000-25,000 (US$600-1,500), not US$5,000. For older travelers: (1) JUST SAY NO at Diamante / Costera resort welcome desks — 'free breakfast + credit' offers are timeshare pitches in disguise; (2) IF attending, set 90-min HARD STOP and stand to leave regardless of tactics; (3) NEVER authorize credit-card 'holds' or 'deposits' during presentation; (4) Mexican 5-business-day cooling-off period is LAW — file PROFECO (profeco.gob.mx) + registered mail to property's legal department within window if you signed; (5) CRITICAL: 'Acapulco rebuilding investment' is high-risk speculative — Hurricane Otis (Cat 5, October 2023) destroyed huge infrastructure; recovery is ongoing; cartel-violence safety overlay makes Acapulco real estate a poor investment for casual buyers; (6) for genuine Mexican property, consult a LICENSED Mexican real-estate attorney (NOT the resort's 'legal counsel') with verifiable Notario Público; (7) REFUSE any 'fideicomiso admin US$5,000' — real range is US$600-1,500; (8) US Consulate Acapulco closed 2024 — nearest US Consulate is Mexico City Embassy +52 55 8526 2561; (9) traveler reports from 2025 confirm that 'travel agencies' approaching at hotel are essentially always timeshare-pitch organizations. How to avoid: JUST SAY NO at Diamante / Costera resort welcome desks If attending, 90-min hard stop; stand and walk out regardless of tactics NEVER authorize credit-card 'holds' or 'deposits' Mexican 5-day cooling-off: file PROFECO if signed For property, consult licensed Mexican real-estate attorney; refuse 'investment' speculation

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — Acapulco Costera Restaurant Tourist-Menu & 'Mariscos Market Price' Padding (tourist-trap, severity: moderate). Acapulco's Costera Miguel Alemán beachfront restaurant strip and Diamante mall dining hosts a 2025 tourist-menu bill-padding ecosystem common to Mexican beach destinations. Traveler reports from 2025 cover the broader Acapulco scam landscape, and 2024 cruise-day reports document dining patterns. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Costera beachfront restaurants with USD-only menus at 2-3x local prices (huachinango fish dish US$30+ vs MX$200-300 at working-class spots); (b) 'mariscos market price' verbal quotes for shrimp/lobster/fish without weight × price/kg disclosed — bills run MX$1,500-3,500; (c) 'gratuity 18%' pre-added + tip line (double-tipping); (d) 'credit-card processing 10-15%' announced at bill; (e) 'complimentary chips/guacamole' arriving as MX$280 line item; (f) 'fresh coconut water US$8' from beach-vendor at restaurant when fair MX$30-50; (g) USD-priced menus padding 10-15% exchange; (h) 'live mariachi service charge MX$100/person' added unannounced; (i) 'special seafood platter market price' that's whatever they decide to charge; (j) Acapulco Old-town zócalo restaurants charging Diamante prices to cruise tourists. For older travelers: (1) eat at AUTHENTIC Acapulco spots: La Cabaña de Caleta (Caleta beach, Mexican seafood, Google 4.6+, MX$250-450), El Cabrito (Costera, traditional Mexican, MX$200-400), 100% Natural (Costera multi-locations, healthier MX$150-300), Becco al Mare (Costera Italian, transparent MX$300-500 per person); (2) for shrimp/seafood, agree weight × price/kg IN WRITING before cooking — fair shrimp MX$400-600/kg, lobster MX$1,000-1,500/kg, fish MX$200-400/kg depending on type; (3) INSPECT bill — refuse 'gratuity 18% + tip' double-dipping; confirm card surcharge 0-3% BEFORE ordering; (4) request MX$ bill (not USD); (5) REFUSE uninvited 'complimentary' appetizers (always charged); (6) for budget eats, Mercado Central de Acapulco (Old Acapulco) has authentic seafood at MX$80-150 per meal; (7) refuse 'live mariachi service charge' — if you want music, agree per-song MX$100-200 with the musicians directly; (8) coconut water from beach vendor: MX$30-50 fair (NEVER US$8 in MX$ pesos). How to avoid: Authentic: La Cabaña de Caleta, El Cabrito, 100% Natural, Becco al Mare Seafood: weight × price/kg IN WRITING; fair shrimp MX$400-600/kg Inspect bill; refuse double-tipping; card 0-3% Mercado Central de Acapulco for budget MX$80-150 Mariachi: agree per-song MX$100-200 with musicians directly

Scam alert in Acapulco, Mexico — Acapulco Beach Vendor & 'Free Massage' Aggressive Pressure Scam (tourist-trap, severity: moderate). Acapulco's public beaches host an active 2025 vendor culture with aggressive pressure tactics. Traveler reports from 2025 cover the broader pitch-pressure context, and cruise-day and visit reports confirm the same landscape. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) beach vendors walking up every 30-60 seconds offering sarongs, jewelry, hair-braids, henna tattoos, parasailing, jet-ski, banana-boat — aggressive 'special price my friend' opening; (b) 'free henna tattoo' that becomes MX$400 when you try to leave; (c) 'massage on the beach MX$300 for 60 min' becoming MX$1,200 'extended deluxe' bill; (d) 'parasail US$80' (legitimate operators MX$700-900 = US$40-50 with comparison-shopping); (e) 'banana-boat ride MX$500 per person' (real MX$200-300); (f) 'photo with iguana / parrot / macaw MX$300-500' (wildlife welfare concern + mass-overcharged); (g) 'beach chair rental US$25' at FREE public sand; (h) 'fresh fruit cup MX$80' (real MX$25-40 from licensed vendors); (i) 'mariachi serenade MX$500 for 3 songs' that becomes MX$1,500 with 'tip expected'; (j) 'safety surveillance fee US$10/day' from fake 'beach security' (no such fee). For older travelers: (1) firm 'no gracias' and keep walking; don't stop, smile, or engage beach vendors; (2) all Mexican beaches are PUBLIC federal property — no entrance fee, no chair-rental obligation, no 'safety fee'; legitimate beach clubs have posted price boards; (3) REFUSE every 'free' offer — henna, massage, photos, fruit, drinks; (4) for parasail, jet-ski, banana-boat, COMPARISON-SHOP 3+ operators on the beach; legitimate rates: parasail MX$600-900 (10-15 min), jet-ski MX$700-1,000 (30 min), banana-boat MX$200-300 per person; (5) for massage, book at hotel spa or Spa Diamante / Spa Pacha at MX$800-1,500 for proper 60-90 min; (6) REFUSE 'photo with exotic animal' — wildlife-welfare violation + 100% scam; (7) take photos yourself with phone timer; never hand phone to 'photographer' tout; (8) for fresh fruit, buy at Mercado Central or licensed beach vendor with posted prices MX$25-40 per cup; (9) refuse 'beach safety fee' — illegitimate; (10) Caleta and Caletilla (Old Acapulco) are calmer than Costera Hornos for older travelers; pier-shuttle to Roqueta Island is MX$70 round-trip if you want a beach day-trip from Old Acapulco. How to avoid: Firm 'no gracias' and keep walking; no engagement Beaches are PUBLIC — no entry fee, no chair-rental obligation Comparison-shop 3+ operators: parasail MX$600-900, jet-ski MX$700-1,000 Massage at hotel spa or Spa Diamante MX$800-1,500 (not beach) REFUSE 'exotic animal photos'; refuse 'beach safety fee' demands

Scam alert in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico — Cabo San Lucas Airport (SJD) 'Shark Tank' Timeshare & Fake Taxi Ambush (transport, severity: high). Los Cabos International Airport (SJD) has Mexico's most-documented 2025 'Shark Tank' airport-timeshare ambush, nearly identical to PVR. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'Shark Tank' right after customs — timeshare salespeople in polos posing as 'tourist information' asking 'Where are you staying?'; (b) 'free shuttle to your resort' lock-in pressure attending 90-min-to-5-hour presentation; (c) 'authorized taxi' kiosks quoting US$80–$150 for Cabo San Lucas transfer (real Uber US$40–$70); (d) fake 'resort welcome agents' with clipboards and name-badges intercepting at Terminal 1; (e) Uber is legal in Los Cabos but with PICKUP RULES — meet driver at specific signposted Uber pickup zone (not curbside); (f) 'combined shuttle + welcome package' bait where the 'welcome package' is a presentation; (g) Garza Blanca (yes, same resort brand as PV) runs similar airport-based intake. For older travelers: (1) WALK STRAIGHT through the Shark Tank — don't stop, don't engage, don't answer 'Where staying?'; (2) book Uber on airport Wi-Fi AFTER exiting terminal — meet at signposted Uber pickup zone (varies by terminal, ask signage); typical SJD to Cabo San Lucas MX$900–$1,500 via Uber (40 km, 45 min drive); to San José del Cabo MX$300–$500 (10 km, 20 min); (3) official shared shuttle (Cabo Yellow Bus, Transcabo) at US$20–$30 per person is LEGITIMATE budget option; (4) if your hotel genuinely includes airport shuttle, verify driver's sign (hotel logo + your name) via WhatsApp before departure; (5) REFUSE every 'free shuttle' offer in Shark Tank; (6) Garza Blanca, Pueblo Bonito, Hilton Los Cabos presentations are 3-5 hours — refuse airport-side engagement; (7) US Consulate Cabo San Lucas +52 624 143 3566. How to avoid: WALK STRAIGHT through Shark Tank; don't engage Book Uber at signposted pickup zone: SJD-Cabo MX$900–$1,500 Official shared shuttle (Cabo Yellow Bus, Transcabo) US$20–$30 pp Verify hotel shuttle sign (logo + your name) via WhatsApp US Consulate Cabo +52 624 143 3566

Scam alert in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico — Cabo San Lucas Marina Tour Boat & 'Private Yacht' Overcharge Scam (tourist-trap, severity: moderate). Cabo's Marina hosts Mexico's highest-volume boat-tour industry — Arch of Cabo sunset cruises, Lovers Beach / Divorce Beach transfers, whale-watching (Dec–Apr), snorkel tours — and hosts a 2025 overcharge + unlicensed-operator ecosystem. Legitimate fares: Arch of Cabo (El Arco) + Lovers Beach water taxi US$20–$30 per person round-trip via Cabo Water Taxi (official); sunset cruise US$60–$90 per person via Cabo Rey Sailing or Cabo Escape; whale-watching (Dec–Apr) US$60–$90 per person group tour; full-day snorkel tour US$80–$120 per person. The 2025 scams: (a) Marina dock touts selling 'private yacht Arco tour US$400 per person' when group tour is US$30; (b) 'VIP sunset cruise with open bar US$250 per person' where 'open bar' is 2 watered-down drinks; (c) 'private whale-watching US$800 per boat' when group tour is US$80; (d) unlicensed 'water taxi' without life jackets at Medano Beach US$50 pp when official US$20; (e) 'Lovers Beach exclusive access US$100' (beach is public); (f) 'pirate cruise' with 'free drinks' that include MX$500 'service fee'; (g) off-season whale-watching offers (May–Nov) — whales have migrated; impossible. For older travelers: (1) for El Arco + Lovers Beach visit, use OFFICIAL Cabo Water Taxi (yellow boats with CoBox or 'Cabo Water Taxi' branding) at US$20–$30 pp round-trip; (2) sunset cruises: book Google 4.7+ operators (Cabo Rey Sailing, Cabo Escape Cruise, Buccaneer Queen) at US$60–$90 pp; (3) whale-watching ONLY December–April — reject 'off-season whale' offers as fraud; book reputable Cabo Adventures, Cabo Expeditions at US$60–$90 pp; (4) REFUSE 'private yacht' upsells — group tours are same experience at 1/10th cost; (5) VERIFY life jackets on boat BEFORE boarding; (6) Lovers Beach is PUBLIC Mexican federal property — no 'exclusive access' fee legitimate; (7) for older travelers, morning water-taxi (less wind) is better than afternoon; bring seasickness meds; (8) traveler reports have specific 2025 pricing references. How to avoid: Cabo Water Taxi (yellow boats) US$20–$30 round-trip to Arco/Lovers Sunset cruise: Cabo Rey, Cabo Escape, Buccaneer Queen at US$60–$90 Whale-watching ONLY Dec–Apr; Cabo Adventures, Cabo Expeditions US$60–$90 REFUSE 'private yacht' upsells; group tours = same experience Verify life jackets BEFORE boarding; seasickness meds

Scam alert in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico — Cabo Timeshare High-Pressure at Pueblo Bonito, Garza Blanca & Villa Group (tourist-trap, severity: high). Cabo San Lucas hosts some of Mexico's most aggressive 2025 timeshare presentation operations, with Pueblo Bonito and Garza Blanca specifically community-named. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) resort welcome desk 'Explore rewards' Pueblo Bonito-style incentive — 'US$200 resort credit + free dinner + spa voucher' for 'preview presentation'; (b) Garza Blanca 'Elite Preview' at 3-5 hour high-pressure sale with mortgage-style commitments US$30,000–$150,000; (c) Villa Group 'written goals' psychological manipulation (same as PV); (d) 'deposit today US$5,000 secures discount' binding-authorisation trap; (e) 'manager' rotation when you decline; (f) 'closer' with 'financial advice' cast as 'helping you plan your retirement'; (g) airport partnership where Shark Tank agents specifically route you to their brand's presentation; (h) 'wife-and-husband must both attend or deal void' separation tactic. For older travelers: (1) JUST SAY NO at Pueblo Bonito, Garza Blanca, Villa Group welcome desks — 'Explore rewards' and 'Elite Preview' are timeshare presentations; (2) if attending, 90-min hard stop; stand up to leave regardless of tactics; (3) NEVER authorize credit-card deposits or 'holds'; (4) NEVER write 'personal goals' or 'retirement plans'; (5) 'Wife-and-husband must both attend' is a separation tactic — if uncomfortable, all leave together; (6) Mexican 5-business-day cooling-off period is LAW — file cancellation via PROFECO + registered mail to property's legal department within window; (7) traveler reports document specific 2025 property exit strategies; (8) if you're harassed or locked in a closing room, firm 'llamo a la policía' (I'm calling police) usually ends the session; (9) US Consulate Cabo +52 624 143 3566 for genuine coercion; (10) a legitimate Cabo vacation can be done WITHOUT any timeshare engagement — Hilton Los Cabos, Hyatt Ziva, JW Marriott all allow pleasant stays without presentation pressure if you avoid welcome desks.
